description: Trying to include innovative and aspiring people.
summary: Mission Architect, built by team BUG E, is a browser game where students design and fly a complete space mission. Players choose a destination (Moon, Mars or Europa), a launch vehicle, a power system, an antenna, science instruments and a propellant load. Live meters show how each choice changes cost, launch mass, delta-v, power and data return. The game then simulates launch, cruise, orbit insertion and science operations, with risks such as launch failure and solar storms, and gives a score. It makes mission trade-offs concrete: bigger rockets cost more, extra propellant adds mass, solar power fades far from the Sun, and distant missions return less data. Failures teach as much as successes, so players can redesign and try again.
details: The game is a single HTML, CSS and JavaScript file with no backend. It uses the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation for delta-v, inverse-square solar flux for power at each destination, and a link-budget-style limit on data return. Players balance a fixed budget, launcher capacity, instrument power draw and communication capacity. Each mission faces probabilistic events, so the same design can succeed or fail. The score rewards science return and unspent budget. It is aimed at students who rarely get to see a whole mission from concept to operation, and it works on phones and laptops with nothing to install.
